method: Evidence/rights gates first. Placement blends interest, relevance, novelty, familiarity, consequence, source confidence, originality, visual strength, freshness, radar context and rotation pressure, then applies a diversity rerank so nearby homepage slots prefer different categories and subjects. Editorial story-overrides are applied before ranking so approved headlines and imagery persist across generated homepage surfaces.

feature.headline: Which Burlington intersection is actually the worst?
feature.deck: The public records point to a larger problem along one of Burlington's busiest roads.
feature.label: Road safety
feature.alt: Illustration of a damaged car and motorcycle at an intersection; not a photograph of a collision discussed in this article.
feature.storyGoal: Use collision counts, red-light camera totals and engineering records to explain why Burlington's worst intersection changes by the measure used, and why different problems keep appearing along Guelph Line.

feature.headline: Burlington spent more than $90 million on stormwater upgrades. Did it work?
feature.deck: Tuck Creek is one place to see what changed after 2014, and what remains unfinished.
feature.label: Infrastructure
feature.alt: Flooding in Burlington during a major rain event.
feature.storyGoal: Explain what Burlington's more than $90 million in stormwater investment has physically changed, using Tuck Creek as a concrete example while being explicit about unfinished and paused work.

feature.headline: Up to 90% of a building can now be made inside this Burlington factory.
feature.deck: A $15-million Canadian hub is changing how some schools, homes and care buildings could be assembled.
feature.label: Made in Burlington
feature.alt: A building under construction in an industrial factory setting.
feature.storyGoal: Turn a new investment announcement into an understandable Made in Burlington story about what the factory makes, how much work can happen indoors and the scale SEKISUI says it is targeting.

rail.headline: Oakville approved a new Costco near Burloak. How will drivers get in?
rail.deck: The site sits close to the Burlington border, with a large parking plan and several proposed access points.
rail.label: Development
rail.alt: Costco storefront and entrance in a suburban shopping area.
rail.storyGoal: Explain the recently approved Costco site plan near Burloak through the practical questions Burlington drivers care about: status, parking, access and what is still unconfirmed.
